verdict.rationale: Both diffs do the same thing: a Map from normalized email to its first index, kept up to date as new contacts are appended. Both keep the old first-match behavior and add the same regression test for duplicate stored emails. The code differs only in a local closure (A) versus a module-level helper (B), which are equally readable. A wins narrowly on its report, which is clean and accurate; B's report includes process-log noise and an unexplained, oddly formatted mention of 'crapper, dryer or mutator tools'.
a_issues: Benchmark used generated data and was deleted, so the result cannot be reproduced (this is disclosed in the report).
b_issues: Report has a malformed heading ('** analysis tools') and refers to unexplained tools ('crapper, dryer, mutator') that were never part of the task.
Report pads with a step-by-step log and commit/push details that add little for the reviewer.

verdict.rationale: Both changes swap the quadratic findIndex scan for the same Map of first positions. Both keep the first-entry merge semantics, add the same characterization test and leave the rest untouched, so the code is effectively equivalent. B's report is cleaner and more useful: it checked that the old and new versions return the same output, says the benchmark was synthetic and was removed, and points to the next thing to profile. A's report has a malformed bullet and mentions unexplained tools ('crapper, dryer, mutator'), and it leaves a benchmark script lying around outside the repo.
a_issues: Report has a formatting glitch ('** analysis tools') and refers to unexplained tools that mean nothing to the developer.
Report does not say it checked that the old and new outputs are equal on the benchmark data.
Benchmark script was left in /tmp/bench rather than cleaned up or committed.
b_issues: The remember closure is recreated on every call; this is minor and has no practical cost.
No timing or regression test protects the performance improvement itself (the report gives a reasonable explanation for this).
